name: Chapter 60B, Article 1. Donated Drug Repository Program.
scope: article W. Va. Code ch. 60B art. 1 (West Virginia Legislature, article PDFs)

notice.label: Notice before it is used on a person

hearing.label: A chance to answer before the decision is final

appeal.label: A way to a court or an independent reviewer

access.label: The person can see the record

standing.label: The person can enforce it themselves

self-report.label: The law must report its own effects

waiver.label: Who can waive it; does it expire
waiver.quote: (a) A donor or eligible recipient may request a waiver or variance from the board with regard to any rule related to this program upon a showing that such action would be in the interest of public health and safety.

boundary.label: What it takes from you, and the limits on that
boundary.quote_takes: (k) A donor or eligible recipient may contract with one another or a third-party to create and/or maintain records on each other’s behalf.
boundary.quote_limits: (5) If applicable, the donor shall remove or redact any patient names and prescription numbers on donated drugs or otherwise maintain patient confidentiality by executing a confidentiality agreement with the eligible recipient.

plain-words.label: Can an ordinary reader follow it
plain-words.quote_longest: “Donor” means any person, including an individual member of the public, or any entity legally authorized to possess drugs with a license or permit in good standing in the state in which it is located, including, but not limited to, a wholesaler or distributor, third party logisti

fair-exchange.label: What a person gives, and what a person gets
fair-exchange.quote_gives: (a) An eligible recipient may not charge or collect any fees from an eligible patient for drugs dispensed pursuant to this program.
fair-exchange.quote_gets: That patient shall be provided with appropriate counseling on the use of the prescription drug, including any potential side effects and the fact that the drug was donated.
